correctness.rationale: For an independent standard Gaussian score vector, constrained bases use r X-coordinates or r-1 X and one Y, giving exact support h_P=sum_{j<=r-1}X_(j)+max(X_(r),Y_(1)), while h_Delta is top r pooled. The support deficit is an integral of binomial exceedance probabilities, strictly positive for q>=2. Gaussian extreme value point processes give joint independent upper/lower order-statistics, with X arrival variables -log Gamma_j, Y max log rho-log E*. Orthogonal projection subtracts a common coordinate mean from both support values; random spherical normalization sqrt(d)/||G_E|| tends to 1 with negligible order a_p correction because log(p)/sqrt(p)->0. Fixed-order normal maxima have uniformly integrable centered tails, so expectation limits follow; the gamma-exponential integral E[log(rho Gamma_r/E*)]_+ has exact expression log(1+rho)+sum[1-(1+rho)^(-j)]/j. The hypersimplex Poisson shift is r log(1+rho), yielding D_r and derivative. Independent exhaustive finite greedy maximization over 150 random problems and 16 numerical gamma-integral identities agreed with formulas. No finite check substitutes for the limit law or uniform-integrability argument.

value.rationale: Mean width is an intrinsic Euclidean geometric invariant; the complete distribution and positive second-order deficit quantify a meaningful loss under the panhandle matroid basis restriction. A fixed-rank family with explicit rho dependence generalizes beyond rank-two exceptional cases and supplies a reproducible extreme-value interpretation.

final_claim: For fixed rank r>=3, p>=r, q>=2 with p->infty and q/p->rho in (0,infty), the spherical directional width of panhandle base polytope centered at 2r u_p and scaled a_p/sqrt(p+q-1) converges to a sum of two independent Poisson-order-statistic random variables. The scaled mean width deficit relative to uniform hypersimplex is D_r(rho)=(r-1)log(1+rho)-sum_{j=1}^{r-1}[1-(1+rho)^(-j)]/j, positive, monotone and with quadratic onset r(r-1)rho²/4.
